findings.text: follow-on: the ready line's largest-reach trio is cut with TOP_WIRING_FINDINGS (declared at line 39 for the wiring-finding count) rather than a reach constant, so one name stands for two unrelated limits and a reader of line 359 reads a wiring name where a reach limit is meant; retuning either limit silently moves the other.

follow-on: --since is declared on the roadmap verb but read only inside the --brief branch at line 1578, so `reckon roadmap --project X --since <ts>` prints the ordinary report and exits 0; the option is silently inert without --brief, where the surrounding verb's idiom (--max-paths, --json-output) is that a supplied option does something or is refused.

follow-on: project_brief raises ValueError when the composed text exceeds BRIEF_CHAR_BUDGET (reckon/project_brief.py:102) and the new CLI path neither catches it nor converts it, so a project whose payload overfills the budget prints a traceback and no ClickException message, unlike the surrounding verb which wraps a failed read at line 1570.

follow-on: no test in the diff reaches _print_roadmap_brief or the --brief option; tests/test_one_brief_an_agent_can_act_on.py exercises project_brief only with a payload passed in, so the surface the plan names (docs/plans/a-project-reads-as-one-picture.html:111) is unguarded and a regression that passed the wrong report or dropped the portfolio branch would leave the gate green.

follow-on: the section's done-when requires the power_convertor brief to name 'the run blocked since 2026-10-17', and the landed brief names r-20261021T161941406279-integrated-assembly-stability blocked since 2026-10-21T16:20:57Z (brief-power_convertor.log); the node's dispatch done-when dropped the date to 'its oldest blocked run' and its manifest records the plan example as stale rather than reconciled, so the plan's worked example still asserts a head and a date the live mount no longer reports.

follow-on: the gate log's first line names revision 83945c06f59bcb50e2151cf9a3e23b9b67cdca2a, at which reckon/project_brief.py — the module under test — does not exist, so the literal command on line 5 of the same log cannot be re-run at the named revision and reproduce the recorded `71 passed`; the tree and measurement_module lines below it name the worktree, which is what actually disambiguates the receipt.
